case_name: Ramaotar v State of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

3 November 1992
Cr.A. No. 302 of 1982 (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 29 September 1981 of the Madhya Pradesh High Court in Cr. A. No. 334 of 1980)
The Judgment was delivered by: G. N. RAY, J.
1.  This appeal is directed against the judgment passed by the Indore Bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court in Criminal Appeal No. 334 of 1980 arising out of the conviction and sentence passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Indore in Sessions Trial 34 of 1980. The appellant along with Kailash, Premchand, Mahesh and Kanhaiya were committed to trial before the learned first Additional Sessions Judge, Indore in Sessions Trial No. 34 of 1980 for offence punishable under Section 148 and Section 302 read with Section 149 IPC. The appellant Ramaotar is the father of other accused Prem Chand, Mahesh and Kanhaiya. Accused 2 Kailash however was not related to Ramaotar. The prosecution case in short is that on November 7, 1979 at about
facts: The prosecution case is that on November 7, 1979 at about 11.30 p.m., when Kamal Singh was not in the house, the appellant had thrown stones at the house of Kamal Singh.
Accused 3 Prem Chand was armed with sword and other accused persons had lathis with them.
The said accused persons abused Ashok and Vijay and challenged them.
Vimlabai (deceased) came out of the house and the appellant Ramaotar assaulted her with a lathi.
Thereafter, all the accused persons started assaulting Vijay and Ashok.
After investigation, the accused persons were arrested and sent up for trial.
issues: Whether Ramaotar had caused injuries on the vital parts of the body and injuries caused on the head and on the ribs of the deceased were attributable only to Ramaotar.
Whether there was any justification for Ramaotar in using the lathi against the sons of Kamal Singh.
petitioner_arguments: Ramaotar himself suffered serious injuries in the hands of sons of Kamal Singh.
There was no intention to kill Vimlabai, but lathi blows on vital parts of the body were dealt only to give a good thrashing.
Vijay had caused injuries on Ramaotar by way of self-defence.
respondent_arguments: The deceased Vimlabai had been necessarily beaten by all the accused persons causing multiple injuries on her person.
Ramaotar hit her on the head which caused a serious injury on the vital parts of her body, and such injury was sufficient to cause death in the ordinary course of nature.
court_reasoning: Although in the first information report, it was specifically mentioned by Ashok the brother of Vijay, that Vijay had caused injuries on the person of Ramaotar by way of self-defence the prosecution witnesses including Vijay attempted to deny such facts of assault accused on the person of Ramaotar.
It appears to us that it was not reasonably expected that the wife of Kamal Singh namely deceased Vimlabai would come out of the house at the dead of night.
holding: The High Court rightly came to the finding that Ramaotar was liable to be punished under Section 302 IPC.
No interference is called for in this appeal and the conviction and sentence should be upheld by this Court.
